sources.title: RFC 6749 — OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework
sources.author: IETF
sources.content: OAuth 2.0 enables a third-party application to obtain limited access to an HTTP service through roles including resource owner, client, authorization server, and resource server. The authorization-code flow separates user authorization from token issuance.

sources.title: RFC 7636 — Proof Key for Code Exchange
sources.author: IETF
sources.content: PKCE mitigates authorization-code interception by binding the authorization request to a high-entropy code verifier. The client sends a derived code challenge first and proves possession of the verifier during token exchange.

sources.title: Matthew Wright — RIT Cybersecurity
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: Matthew Wright is chair and professor of cybersecurity with expertise in security, privacy, cyber analytics, adversarial machine learning, and usable security, and teaches Authentication and Security Models.
